entities.summary: Laodice of Cappadocia (fl. 116 BC) was a princess from the Kingdom of Pontus and a queen of the Kingdom of Cappadocia by marriage to Ariarathes VI, and queen of Bithynia by marriage to Nicomedes III. She played a pivotal role in the governance of Cappadocia during the minority of her son Ariarathes VII, showcasing her strategic prowess as regent. Laodice's tenure was marked by political intrigue, as she navigated the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the Hellenistic kingdoms. Her leadership during this period had a lasting impact on the regional dynamics, as she skillfully managed the interests of her kingdom and secured key victories against rival powers. Laodice of Cappadocia's legacy extends beyond her own time, as her experiences and decisions influenced the trajectory of the Hellenistic world, leaving a lasting testament to her intelligence, cunning, and political acumen.
